test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 21 Oct, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In which of the following cases did the Supreme Court of India propound the Basic Structure Doctrine of the Constitution?

options.text: Kesavanand Bharti vs. State of Kerala Case
Maneka Gandhi vs Union of India Case
Golaknath vs. State of Punjab Case
Indira Gandhi vs. Raj Narayan Case

solution:
The correct answer is __**Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala Case**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala** case (1973) is a landmark judgment by the Supreme Court of India where the **Basic Structure Doctrine** was propounded.
 
• This doctrine asserts that **certain fundamental features of the Constitution cannot be amended by the Parliament**.
 
• The case arose when Kesavananda Bharati, a religious leader, challenged the Kerala government’s attempts to impose restrictions on his property under land reform laws.
 
• The Supreme Court ruled by a narrow majority of 7:6 that while Parliament has wide powers to amend the Constitution under Article 368, it **cannot alter its basic structure**.
 
• This doctrine ensures that the core principles of the Constitution, such as **democracy, secularism, federalism, and the rule of law**, remain intact.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Basic Structure Doctrine:**

 
 
• It is a judicial principle that limits the amending power of Parliament to ensure the Constitution's basic features are preserved.
 
• Examples of basic structure elements include the supremacy of the Constitution, independence of the judiciary, and the secular character of the state.
 
 
 
• **Article 368:**
 
 
• It deals with the powers and procedure of Parliament to amend the Constitution.
 
• The Kesavananda Bharati case clarified that this power is not absolute and is subject to judicial review.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Review:**
 
 
• The power of the judiciary to examine the constitutionality of legislative acts and executive orders.
 
• The Basic Structure Doctrine strengthens judicial review as a safeguard against unconstitutional amendments.
 
 
 
• **Other Related Cases:**
 
 
• **Golaknath vs. State of Punjab (1967):** Held that fundamental rights cannot be amended under Article 368.
 
• **Indira Gandhi vs. Raj Narayan (1975):** Applied the Basic Structure Doctrine to strike down the 39th Amendment.
 
• **Minerva Mills vs. Union of India (1980):** Reaffirmed the Basic Structure Doctrine, emphasizing the balance between fundamental rights and directive principles.
